ttd.basisLabel: Gross average weekly wage before taxes
ttd.rateText: Sixty-six and two-thirds percent of the wages received at the time of injury, not more than the maximum and not less than the minimum weekly income benefit of § 48-121.01 (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 48-121(1)); the maximum is 100% of the state average weekly wage rounded to the next higher dollar (§ 48-121.01(1)(b)).
ttd.minText: Minimum weekly income benefit of $49 (§ 48-121.01(2)); a worker earning less than $49 a week receives his or her full wages (§ 48-121(1)).

waiting.text: Indemnity benefits begin on the eighth calendar day of disability after a seven-day waiting period; if disability continues six weeks or longer, the waiting week is paid after six weeks elapse (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 48-119; Court FAQ).

ttdDuration.text: Total disability compensation is paid during the disability, with no fixed week cap (§ 48-121(1)); temporary benefits usually end at maximum medical improvement or release from care (Court FAQ). Partial disability is limited to 300 weeks (§ 48-121(2)).

ppd.text: Scheduled members are paid at 66-2/3% of wages for fixed periods in addition to temporary disability (e.g. thumb 60 weeks, index finger 35 weeks) (§ 48-121(3)); body-as-a-whole injuries are paid on loss of earning capacity at 66-2/3% of the wage difference for up to 300 weeks (§ 48-121(2); Court FAQ).

facts.text: Before each new year the Governor may hold a public hearing and suspend the automatic increase of the maximum weekly benefit (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 48-121.01(1)(b)).
Nebraska's minimum weekly benefit is a fixed $49 in statute, not indexed to wages; the section was last amended in 1993 (§ 48-121.01(2), source note Laws 1993, LB 757).
The employer must tell the worker of the right to choose as treating physician a doctor who has treated the worker or a family member; if the worker does not choose, the employer selects (Court FAQ).
From July 1, 2026 the burial benefit is $12,200.00 and medical mileage is reimbursed at 76.0 cents per mile (Court benefit rates page).
Loss of two scheduled members in one accident is treated as permanent total disability (Court FAQ).
